rubric.evidence: Behavior description quotes the chromestatus API summary verbatim (effect-tree traversal to the highest ancestor without SVG filters). The normative rule is quoted from the actual spec PR patch (w3c/csswg-drafts#13846, fetched via patch-diff): 'User agents must not apply SVG reference filters to cross-origin/restricted iframes or web plugins because of their ability to arbitrarily manipulate pixels.' The filter grammar (filter: none | <filter-value-list>; <filter-value-list> = [ <filter-function> | <url> ]+) and the <url> reference-filter definition were extracted verbatim from drafts.csswg.org/filter-effects-1 on 2026-07-26. TAG-review quote ('disabling one we perhaps should not have supported') is from the feature detail. No API members exist to invent — the page documents a restriction.

Feature id 5117170452398080 appears in features_by_type for milestone=150 under 'Enabled by default' (listing fetched 2026-07-26). Slug 'disable-svg-filters-on-plugins-and-iframes' derived from the LISTING name via the server slugify.

7 h2-level parts: baseline banner, behavior-change warn-block, at a glance, What changed and why (both attack classes with primary sources), Syntax (grammar + scope of the restriction), Examples (live embed + attack-shape snippet), Browser compatibility (interim, per-vendor with standards-position links), Specifications, See also.

Distinguishes SVG reference filters (url()) from <filter-function> shorthands — the key scoping fact for migration. States what is unaffected (same-origin unrestricted iframes) with WebKit's shipped line as precedent. Fallback painting explained in lede, warn-block, and at-a-glance.

Live showcase concept embedded (filter-comparison, HEAD-checked 200; policy-tester/clickjacking-replay/sandbox-filter-test linked in See also). Full-page headless-Chrome screenshot read: the iframe renders the real demo (Filter Comparison heading, Filter ON/OFF controls, same-origin vs cross-origin cards), not a blank box. Snippet shows the attack shape the restriction defuses, composed from spec syntax with citation.

No BCD entry and no webstatus.dev web-features entry (both checked 2026-07-26) — the page says so and labels the table interim. Safari's shipped-equivalent nuance (allows same-origin iframes) and Firefox's current allow-all behavior come from the notes on the recorded standards positions (WebKit#654, mozilla#1395), both linked.

chromestatus identity link present (7 occurrences in served DOM). Spec PR, filter-effects draft, lyra.horse write-up, Black Hat PDF, both standards positions, and 4 showcase routes — showcase routes HEAD-checked 200 during build; all target=_blank links carry rel=noopener (suite pass).
